transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today? Is there something specific you'd like to talk about?

Hi. Well, the main reason I'm here is that I'm having a really hard time at work. I'm a registered nurse, and when I'm on the floor, I just... I lose my train of thought constantly. 

It's like, an IV pump will beep, or I'll hear someone ask another nurse a question, or a call light goes off down the hall, and suddenly I've completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was just working on. It happens all the time, and it's making my job really difficult to manage.
Have you always had trouble staying focused, or is this something that started recently? Also, do you find yourself feeling restless or acting without thinking in other areas of your life?

It's definitely not a new thing. I think I've always had trouble with it. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would write notes saying I was bright but careless. I was always losing my worksheets or just completely forgetting to turn in my homework. My mom actually had to sit down with me every single night just to keep me on track so I'd finish anything. 

As for feeling restless or acting without thinking... no, I don't really get like that. It's mostly just the focus and, um, losing my place in whatever I'm doing.
Do you also have trouble staying focused or losing track of things in other parts of your life, like at home or during social activities?

Yeah, it definitely happens outside of work, too. I just... I forget things that should be completely routine. 

Like, I'll completely forget to call a family member back, or I'll miss paying a bill at home. I've even missed appointments just because I forgot to show up. And it's really frustrating because I fully intend to do these things. Sometimes I even set a reminder on my phone, and I still somehow end up forgetting. 

It's the same kind of thing with work, like forgetting to follow up on a missing order. It just feels like I can't keep track of normal, everyday things, no matter how hard I try to stay on top of them.
